sanskrit: evaṃ saṃstambhitaṃ vākyaiḥ kuntyā bahuvidhair manaḥ sahadevasya rājendra rājñaś caiva viśeṣataḥ
english: Thus, O lord of kings, by Kuntī's words of many kinds was the mind of Sahadeva steadied, and most especially that of the king Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: te mātrā samanujñātā rājñā ca kurupuṃgavāḥ abhivādya kuruśreṣṭham āmantrayitum ārabhan
english: Given leave by their mother and by the king, those bulls among the Kurus saluted Yudhiṣṭhira, the best of the Kurus, and began to take their leave.

sanskrit: rājan pratigamiṣyāmaḥ śivena pratinanditāḥ anujñātās tvayā rājan gamiṣyāmo vikalmaṣāḥ
english: "O king, we shall return, blessed by your goodwill; granted leave by you, O king, we shall go forth free of sin."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa rājarṣir dharmarājñā mahātmanā anujajñe jayāśīrbhir abhinandya yudhiṣṭhiram
english: So addressed by the great-souled Dharmarāja, the royal sage gave his leave, greeting Yudhiṣṭhira with blessings of victory.

sanskrit: bhīmaṃ ca balināṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sāntvayām āsa pārthivaḥ sa cāsya samyaṅ medhāvī pratyapadyata vīryavān
english: The king consoled Bhīma too, foremost of the strong; and the wise and valiant Bhīma received his words with full grace.

sanskrit: arjunaṃ ca samāśliṣya yamau ca puruṣarṣabhau anujajñe sa kauravyaḥ pariṣvajyābhinandya ca
english: Embracing Arjuna and the twins, those bulls among men, the Kaurava gave them leave, clasping and greeting them with affection.

sanskrit: gāndhāryā cābhyanujñātāḥ kṛtapādābhivandanāḥ jananyā samupāghrātāḥ pariṣvaktāś ca te nṛpam cakruḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ sarve vatsā iva nivāraṇe
english: Granted leave by Gāndhārī, having bowed at her feet, smelled upon the head and embraced by their mother, they all circled the king to the right, like calves held back from their pen.

sanskrit: punaḥ punar nirīkṣantaḥ prajagmus te pradakṣiṇam tathaiva draupadī sādhvī sarvāḥ kauravayoṣitaḥ
english: Looking back again and again, they walked round him to the right; and so too did the chaste Draupadī and all the women of the Kauravas.

sanskrit: nyāyataḥ śvaśure vṛttiṃ prayujya prayayus tataḥ śvaśrūbhyāṃ samanujñātāḥ pariṣvajyābhinanditāḥ saṃdiṣṭāś cetikartavyaṃ prayayur bhartṛbhiḥ saha
english: Having rendered fitting service to their father-in-law, they set out; given leave by their two mothers-in-law, embraced and greeted, and instructed in their duties, they departed together with their husbands.

sanskrit: tataḥ prajajñe ninadaḥ sūtānāṃ yujyatām iti uṣṭrāṇāṃ krośatāṃ caiva hayānāṃ heṣatām api
english: Then arose the clamor of the charioteers crying "Yoke up!", and of camels bawling and horses neighing.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā sadāraḥ sahasainikaḥ nagaraṃ hāstinapuraṃ punar āyāt sabāndhavaḥ
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, with his wife, with his troops, and with his kinsmen, came back again to the city of Hāstinapura.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dvivarṣopanivṛtteṣu pāṇḍaveṣu yadṛcchayā devarṣir nārado rājann ājagāma yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the Pāṇḍavas had returned, in the second year, O king, the divine sage Nārada came of his own accord to Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tam abhyarcya mahābāhuḥ kururājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ āsīnaṃ pariviśvastaṃ provāca vadatāṃ varaḥ
english: Having honored him, the mighty-armed Kuru king Yudhiṣṭhira, best of speakers, addressed him as he sat at ease and fully at rest.

sanskrit: cirasya khalu paśyāmi bhagavantam upasthitam kaccit te kuśalaṃ vipra śubhaṃ vā pratyupasthitam
english: "After a long time indeed do I see your blessed self come to us. Is all well with you, O brāhmaṇa, and has good fortune attended you?"

sanskrit: ke deśāḥ paridṛṣṭās te kiṃ ca kāryaṃ karomi te tad brūhi dvijamukhya tvam asmākaṃ ca priyo 'tithiḥ
english: "What lands have you visited, and what task may I perform for you? Tell me that, O foremost of the twice-born; you are our welcome guest."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca ciradṛṣṭo 'si me rājann āgato 'smi tapovanāt paridṛṣṭāni tīrthāni gaṅgā caiva mayā nṛpa
english: Nārada said: After long I behold you, O king. I have come from the penance-grove. I have visited the sacred fords, and the Gaṅgā too, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca vadanti puruṣā me 'dya gaṅgātīranivāsinaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ mahātmānam āsthitaṃ paramaṃ tapaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Men dwelling on the banks of the Gaṅgā tell me today that the great-souled Dhṛtarāṣṭra has undertaken the most severe austerities.

sanskrit: api dṛṣṭas tvayā tatra kuśalī sa kurūdvahaḥ gāndhārī ca pṛthā caiva sūtaputraś ca saṃjayaḥ
english: Did you see there in good health that upholder of the Kurus, and Gāndhārī, and Pṛthā, and the charioteer's son Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca vartate cādya pitā mama sa pārthivaḥ śrotum icchāmi bhagavan yadi dṛṣṭas tvayā nṛpaḥ
english: And how fares now my father, that king? I wish to hear, O blessed one, if you have seen the monarch.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca sthirībhūya mahārāja śṛṇu sarvaṃ yathātatham yathā śrutaṃ ca dṛṣṭaṃ ca mayā tasmiṃs tapovane
english: Nārada said: Steady yourself, O great king, and hear all just as it is, as it was heard and seen by me in that penance-grove.

sanskrit: vanavāsanivṛtteṣu bhavatsu kurunandana kurukṣetrāt pitā tubhyaṃ gaṅgādvāraṃ yayau nṛpa
english: When you had returned from your sojourn in the forest, O delight of the Kurus, your father went from Kurukṣetra to the Gate of the Gaṅgā, O king.

sanskrit: gāndhāryā sahito dhīmān vadhvā kuntyā samanvitaḥ saṃjayena ca sūtena sāgnihotraḥ sayājakaḥ
english: The wise one, together with Gāndhārī, accompanied by his daughter-in-law Kuntī, and by the charioteer Saṃjaya, took with him his sacred fires and his priests.

sanskrit: ātasthe sa tapas tīvraṃ pitā tava tapodhanaḥ vīṭāṃ mukhe samādhāya vāyubhakṣo 'bhavan muniḥ
english: Your father, rich in penance, took up fierce austerity; placing a pebble in his mouth, that sage became one who fed on air alone.

sanskrit: vane sa munibhiḥ sarvaiḥ pūjyamāno mahātapāḥ tvagasthimātraśeṣaḥ sa ṣaṇmāsān abhavan nṛpaḥ
english: In the forest, honored by all the sages, that king of great penance, reduced to mere skin and bone, so passed six months.

sanskrit: gāndhārī tu jalāhārā kuntī māsopavāsinī saṃjayaḥ ṣaṣṭhabhaktena vartayām āsa bhārata
english: Gāndhārī subsisted on water, Kuntī fasted for a month at a time, and Saṃjaya sustained himself by taking food only every sixth meal, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: agnīṃs tu yājakās tatra juhuvur vidhivat prabho dṛśyato 'dṛśyataś caiva vane tasmin nṛpasya ha
english: There the officiating priests offered into the king's fires according to the rite, O lord, the king himself being now seen and now unseen in that forest.

sanskrit: aniketo 'tha rājā sa babhūva vanagocaraḥ te cāpi sahite devyau saṃjayaś ca tam anvayuḥ
english: The king then became homeless, ranging the forest; and the two queens together, and Saṃjaya, followed after him.

sanskrit: saṃjayo nṛpater netā sameṣu viṣameṣu ca gāndhāryās tu pṛthā rājaṃś cakṣur āsīd aninditā
english: Saṃjaya was the king's guide over smooth ground and rough; and the blameless Pṛthā, O king, was the eyes of Gāndhārī.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cid gaṅgāyāḥ kacche sa nṛpasattamaḥ gaṅgāyām āpluto dhīmān āśramābhimukho 'bhavat
english: Then once, on the bank of the Gaṅgā, that best of kings, the wise one, having bathed in the Gaṅgā, set his face toward the hermitage.

sanskrit: atha vāyuḥ samudbhūto dāvāgnir abhavan mahān dadāha tad vanaṃ sarvaṃ parigṛhya samantataḥ
english: Then a wind arose and a great forest fire sprang up; it seized and burned that whole wood on every side.

sanskrit: dahyatsu mṛgayūtheṣu dvijihveṣu samantataḥ varāhāṇāṃ ca yūtheṣu saṃśrayatsu jalāśayān
english: As the herds of deer burned all around, and the serpents, and the herds of boars, all taking refuge in the pools of water,

sanskrit: samāviddhe vane tasmin prāpte vyasana uttame nirāhāratayā rājā mandaprāṇaviceṣṭitaḥ asamartho 'pasaraṇe sukṛśau mātarau ca te
english: when that forest was engulfed and this dire calamity had come, the king, his vital movements feeble from fasting, was unable to flee, and so were your two mothers, worn utterly thin.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa nṛpatir dṛṣṭvā vahnim āyāntam antikāt idam āha tataḥ sūtaṃ saṃjayaṃ pṛthivīpate
english: Then that king, seeing the fire drawing near, spoke thus to the charioteer Saṃjaya, O lord of the earth:

sanskrit: gaccha saṃjaya yatrāgnir na tvāṃ dahati karhi cit vayam atrāgninā yuktā gamiṣyāmaḥ parāṃ gatim
english: "Go, Saṃjaya, where the fire may never burn you; we here, joined with this fire, shall go to the supreme goal."

sanskrit: tam uvāca kilodvignaḥ saṃjayo vadatāṃ varaḥ rājan mṛtyur aniṣṭo 'yaṃ bhavitā te vṛthāgninā
english: To him Saṃjaya, best of speakers, much agitated, replied: "O king, this will be an unwished-for death for you, by a fire kindled in vain."

sanskrit: na copāyaṃ prapaśyāmi mokṣaṇe jātavedasaḥ yad atrānantaraṃ kāryaṃ tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: "And I see no means of escape from the fire. What now must be done at once—that you should tell me."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ saṃjayenedaṃ punar āha sa pārthivaḥ naiṣa mṛtyur aniṣṭo no niḥsṛtānāṃ gṛhāt svayam
english: So addressed by Saṃjaya, the king spoke again: "This is no unwished-for death for us, who left our home of our own will."

sanskrit: jalam agnis tathā vāyur atha vāpi vikarśanam tāpasānāṃ praśasyante gaccha saṃjaya māciram
english: "Water, fire, wind, and likewise self-starvation—these are praised for ascetics as ends. Go, Saṃjaya, without delay."

sanskrit: ity uktvā saṃjayaṃ rājā samādhāya manas tadā prāṅmukhaḥ saha gāndhāryā kuntyā copāviśat tadā
english: Having said this to Saṃjaya, the king then composed his mind and sat down facing east, together with Gāndhārī and Kuntī.

sanskrit: saṃjayas taṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā pradakṣiṇam athākarot uvāca cainaṃ medhāvī yuṅkṣvātmānam iti prabho
english: Saṃjaya, seeing him thus, walked round him to the right; and the wise man said to him, "Unite your self in yoga," O lord.

sanskrit: ṛṣiputro manīṣī sa rājā cakre 'sya tad vacaḥ saṃnirudhyendriyagrāmam āsīt kāṣṭhopamas tadā
english: That king, son of a sage and thoughtful, did as he bade; restraining the whole host of his senses, he became then like a log of wood.

sanskrit: gāndhārī ca mahābhāgā jananī ca pṛthā tava dāvāgninā samāyukte sa ca rājā pitā tava
english: And the greatly blessed Gāndhārī, and Pṛthā your mother, and that king your father—all were joined with the forest fire.

sanskrit: saṃjayas tu mahāmātras tasmād dāvād amucyata gaṅgākūle mayā dṛṣṭas tāpasaiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: But the high-minded Saṃjaya escaped from that conflagration; I saw him on the bank of the Gaṅgā, surrounded by ascetics.

sanskrit: sa tān āmantrya tejasvī nivedyaitac ca sarvaśaḥ prayayau saṃjayaḥ sūto himavantaṃ mahīdharam
english: That radiant one, taking leave of them and reporting all this in full, the charioteer Saṃjaya set out for the mountain Himavat.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa nidhanaṃ prāptaḥ kururājo mahāmanāḥ gāndhārī ca pṛthā caiva jananyau te narādhipa
english: Thus did the high-minded Kuru king meet his end, and so too Gāndhārī and Pṛthā, your two mothers, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: yadṛcchayānuvrajatā mayā rājñaḥ kalevaram tayoś ca devyor ubhayor dṛṣṭāni bharatarṣabha
english: Wandering there by chance, I beheld the king's body and the bodies of both those queens, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tatas tapovane tasmin samājagmus tapodhanāḥ śrutvā rājñas tathā niṣṭhāṃ na tv aśocan gatiṃ ca te
english: Then into that penance-grove gathered the ascetics, having heard of the king's end; yet they did not grieve, knowing the goal he and they had attained.

sanskrit: tatrāśrauṣam ahaṃ sarvam etat puruṣasattama yathā ca nṛpatir dagdho devyau te ceti pāṇḍava
english: There I heard all of this, O best of men: how the king was burned, and the two queens as well, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: na śocitavyaṃ rājendra svantaḥ sa pṛthivīpatiḥ prāptavān agnisaṃyogaṃ gāndhārī jananī ca te
english: You should not grieve, O lord of kings; that ruler of the earth came to a good end, attaining union with the fire, as did Gāndhārī and your mother.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā tu sarveṣāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām niryāṇaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya śokaḥ samabhavan mahān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing of the passing of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, great grief arose among all the great-souled Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: antaḥpurāṇāṃ ca tadā mahān ārtasvaro 'bhavat paurāṇāṃ ca mahārāja śrutvā rājñas tadā gatim
english: And then a great cry of anguish went up from the inner apartments and from the townsfolk, O great king, when they heard of the king's end.

sanskrit: aho dhig iti rājā tu vikruśya bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ ūrdhvabāhuḥ smaran mātuḥ praruroda yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhīmasenapurogāś ca bhrātaraḥ sarva eva te
english: "Alas! Shame!" cried King Yudhiṣṭhira, sore stricken with grief; with arms upraised, remembering his mother, he wept aloud, and so did all his brothers, led by Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: antaḥpureṣu ca tadā sumahān ruditasvanaḥ prādurāsīn mahārāja pṛthāṃ śrutvā tathāgatām
english: And then a very great sound of weeping arose in the inner apartments, O great king, when they heard that Pṛthā had so passed away.

sanskrit: taṃ ca vṛddhaṃ tathā dagdhaṃ hataputraṃ narādhipam anvaśocanta te sarve gāndhārīṃ ca tapasvinīm
english: And all of them mourned that aged king, burned thus, whose sons had been slain, and the ascetic Gāndhārī as well.

sanskrit: tasminn uparate śabde muhūrtād iva bhārata nigṛhya bāṣpaṃ dhairyeṇa dharmarājo 'bravīd idam
english: When that clamor had subsided, after a moment, O Bhārata, Dharmarāja, restraining his tears by firmness, spoke these words.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca tathā mahātmanas tasya tapasy ugre ca vartataḥ anāthasyeva nidhanaṃ tiṣṭhatsv asmāsu bandhuṣu
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: That such a great-souled one, engaged in fierce penance, should perish as if helpless, while we his kinsmen yet lived—

sanskrit: durvijñeyā hi gatayaḥ puruṣāṇāṃ matā mama yatra vaicitravīryo 'sau dagdha evaṃ davāgninā
english: hard indeed to fathom, I think, are the destinies of men, when that son of Vicitravīrya was thus burned by the forest fire.

sanskrit: yasya putraśataṃ śrīmad abhavad bāhuśālinaḥ nāgāyutabalo rājā sa dagdho hi davāgninā
english: He whose splendid hundred sons were born to him, the strong-armed king with the might of ten thousand elephants—he it is who was burned by the forest fire.

sanskrit: yaṃ purā paryavījanta tālavṛntair varastriyaḥ taṃ gṛdhrāḥ paryavījanta dāvāgniparikālitam
english: He whom of old the loveliest women fanned with palm-leaf fans—him, scorched by the forest fire, the vultures fanned with their wings.

sanskrit: sūtamāgadhasaṃghaiś ca śayāno yaḥ prabodhyate dharaṇyāṃ sa nṛpaḥ śete pāpasya mama karmabhiḥ
english: He who as he lay was wakened by throngs of bards and minstrels—that king now lies upon the bare earth, through the deeds of my own sin.

sanskrit: na tu śocāmi gāndhārīṃ hataputrāṃ yaśasvinīm patilokam anuprāptāṃ tathā bhartṛvrate sthitām
english: Yet I do not grieve for the illustrious Gāndhārī, her sons slain, who has reached her husband's world, so steadfast in her vow of devotion to her lord.

sanskrit: pṛthām eva tu śocāmi yā putraiśvaryam ṛddhimat utsṛjya sumahad dīptaṃ vanavāsam arocayat
english: But for Pṛthā alone do I grieve, who, casting aside the great and shining sovereignty of her sons, chose instead to dwell in the forest.

sanskrit: dhig rājyam idam asmākaṃ dhig balaṃ dhik parākramam kṣatradharmaṃ ca dhig yasmān mṛtā jīvāmahe vayam
english: Fie on this kingdom of ours, fie on our strength, fie on our valor, and fie on the warrior's code, since we live on while she is dead!

sanskrit: susūkṣmā kila kālasya gatir dvijavarottama yat samutsṛjya rājyaṃ sā vanavāsam arocayat
english: Most subtle indeed is the course of Time, O most excellent of the twice-born, in that she gave up the kingdom and chose to dwell in the forest.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirasya jananī bhīmasya vijayasya ca anāthavat kathaṃ dagdhā iti muhyāmi cintayan
english: The mother of Yudhiṣṭhira, of Bhīma, and of Vijaya—how could she have been burned as though she had no protector? Thinking on it I am bewildered.

sanskrit: vṛthā saṃtoṣito vahniḥ khāṇḍave savyasācinā upakāram ajānan sa kṛtaghna iti me matiḥ
english: In vain, it seems, was the fire gratified at Khāṇḍava by the ambidextrous Arjuna; ungrateful is that fire, heedless of the kindness done it—so I think.

sanskrit: yatrādahat sa bhagavān mātaraṃ savyasācinaḥ kṛtvā yo brāhmaṇacchadma bhikṣārthī samupāgataḥ dhig agniṃ dhik ca pārthasya viśrutāṃ satyasaṃdhatām
english: For there that lord burned the mother of the ambidextrous one—the same who, in the guise of a brāhmaṇa, had once come begging for alms. Fie on that fire, and fie on the renowned fidelity to truth of Pārtha!

sanskrit: idaṃ kaṣṭataraṃ cānyad bhagavan pratibhāti me vṛthāgninā samāyogo yad abhūt pṛthivīpateḥ
english: And this other thing seems to me more grievous still, O blessed one: that the lord of the earth met his end through a fire kindled in vain.

sanskrit: tathā tapasvinas tasya rājarṣeḥ kauravasya ha katham evaṃvidho mṛtyuḥ praśāsya pṛthivīm imām
english: For that ascetic Kaurava royal sage—how could a death of such a kind befall him, who had ruled over this whole earth?

sanskrit: tiṣṭhatsu mantrapūteṣu tasyāgniṣu mahāvane vṛthāgninā samāyukto niṣṭhāṃ prāptaḥ pitā mama
english: Though his fires sanctified by sacred mantras stood there in the great forest, my father met his end joined to a fire kindled in vain.

sanskrit: manye pṛthā vepamānā kṛśā dhamanisaṃtatā hā tāta dharmarājeti samākrandan mahābhaye
english: I imagine Pṛthā, trembling, gaunt, her veins standing out, crying aloud in that great terror, "Alas, my son, O Dharmarāja!"

sanskrit: bhīma paryāpnuhi bhayād iti caivābhivāśatī samantataḥ parikṣiptā mātā me 'bhūd davāgninā
english: And wailing too, "Bhīma, save me from this peril!"—my mother was encircled on every side by the forest fire.

sanskrit: sahadevaḥ priyas tasyāḥ putrebhyo 'dhika eva tu na caināṃ mokṣayām āsa vīro mādravatīsutaḥ
english: Sahadeva was dear to her, dearer even than her own sons; yet that hero, the son of Mādrī, could not deliver her.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā ruruduḥ sarve samāliṅgya parasparam pāṇḍavāḥ pañca duḥkhārtā bhūtānīva yugakṣaye
english: Hearing this, the five Pāṇḍavas all wept, embracing one another, stricken with grief, like beings at the dissolution of an age.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu puruṣendrāṇāṃ rudatāṃ ruditasvanaḥ prāsādābhogasaṃruddho anvarautsīt sa rodasī
english: And the sound of those lords of men weeping, pent up within the vast expanse of the palace, made heaven and earth resound in answer.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca nāsau vṛthāgninā dagdho yathā tatra śrutaṃ mayā vaicitravīryo nṛpatis tat te vakṣyāmi bhārata
english: Nārada said: That king, the son of Vicitravīrya, was not burned by a fire kindled in vain, as I heard there; this I shall tell you, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vanaṃ praviśatā tena vāyubhakṣeṇa dhīmatā agnayaḥ kārayitveṣṭim utsṛṣṭā iti naḥ śrutam
english: As that wise one entered the forest, feeding on air alone, he had a sacrifice performed and then released his fires—so we have heard.

sanskrit: yājakās tu tatas tasya tān agnīn nirjane vane samutsṛjya yathākāmaṃ jagmur bharatasattama
english: His officiating priests then let those fires loose in the lonely forest and went their way as they pleased, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: sa vivṛddhas tadā vahnir vane tasminn abhūt kila tena tad vanam ādīptam iti me tāpasābruvan
english: That fire then grew great in that forest, and by it, they say, the wood was set ablaze—so the ascetics told me.

sanskrit: sa rājā jāhnavīkacche yathā te kathitaṃ mayā tenāgninā samāyuktaḥ svenaiva bharatarṣabha
english: Thus that king, on the bank of the Jāhnavī, as I have told you, was joined with that fire—his own very fire, O bull of the Bhāratas.
